subject: FinCo Performance SLOs — Context Window & Latency Targets
messages:
From: Alex Reynolds <alex.reynolds@finco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lisa Brown <lisa.brown@finco.com>
Date: 2026-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: FinCo Performance SLOs follow-up

Marissa — thanks again for the call this morning. Helpful conversation.

Quick recap of what we're trying to achieve so your team can propose an initial plan and benchmark: 
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end <= 200ms for user-facing completions (streaming preferred).
- Throughput: avg 150 requests/sec at peak 30-min windows (bursty traffic).
- Concurrency: up to 120 concurrent sessions, each issuing a stream of tokens (avg response 400 output tokens).
- Context window: 32k input tokens in the worst case (document + user history). Typical request: 8–12k input tokens.
- Token budget per request: input ~8k–32k, output up to 4k.
- Streaming requirements: must deliver first tokens within 50–70ms and sustain steady token send rate without blocking.

Notes: security/compliance discussion is in a separate thread; for this one, we want to confirm feasibility and get a benchmarking plan and rough sizing estimate.

Can you send a short recap of next steps and what you need from us to run an initial perf test?

— Alex
CTO, FinCo

- Latency: p95 <= 200ms E2E for streaming completions; first token within 50–70ms.
- Throughput: peak ~150 req/s with bursts; concurrency ~120 sessions.
- Context window: up to 32k tokens (worst case), typical 8–12k.
- Output tokens: up to 4k per response (most ~400 tokens).

Questions / clarifications we need before benchmarking:
1) Typical model family (open vs proprietary) you prefer / must use? If open, which variants are you evaluating?
2) Fraction of requests that hit the 32k window vs typical 8–12k (gives us good workload mix).
3) Expected distribution of prompt+response sizes (we can work with a 80/20 mix if helpful).

Proposed next steps:

- Us: validate feasibility, propose a benchmark plan and resource sizing (ETA 48–72 hours after sample data).
- Schedule a short tech sync with our SEs to confirm streaming behavior and deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated).

I'll loop in Neha (solutions eng) and Michael (sales eng) to scope the perf plan and propose an initial config.

Best,

Date: 2026-05-24T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinCo Performance SLOs follow-up — initial technical notes + perf plan

Thanks Marissa / Alex — quick technical readout and recommended next steps. Attaching a short perf plan (perf_benchmark_plan_20260524.pdf).

Initial feasibility 
- Short answer: achievable, but tradeoffs matter. 32k context windows significantly increase memory usage and per-token compute; streaming constraints (first token within ~50–70ms) push us toward lower-latency model variants and dedicated capacity for predictable tail behavior.

Key considerations (high level):
- Context window impact: larger context (32k) means bigger KV cache and attention compute. For autoregressive models, p95 token latency increases roughly linearly with context length for the attention step — expect non-trivial tail increases when many concurrent requests hit the full window.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming adds cost for low-latency first-byte. We need warm KV cache and small initial decode steps to hit the 50–70ms first-token objective. Batching helps throughput but harms first-byte latency; continuous batching and dynamic schedule can mitigate some of this.
- Throughput & concurrency: 150 req/s with 120 concurrent sessions is moderate but when combined with 32k windows you'll need GPU memory headroom. If most requests are 8–12k, we size for the typical case and include a small reserved pool for 32k bursts.
- Model choice & quantization: recommend testing a 16-bit (fp16) variant and an int8 quantized variant if available. Quantization reduces memory/compute for large contexts but can slightly affect per-token latency variability and quality.

Suggested benchmarking plan (overview):
1) Replay mix: 80% typical (8–12k input, 400 output), 20% worst-case (32k input, 4k output).
2) Modes: streaming enabled and disabled (to measure first-byte and sustained throughput).
3) Metrics: p50/p95/p99 E2E latency, first-byte latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory usage, queue depth, percent of requests hitting fallback.
4) Runs: baseline on hosted configuration; dedicated sizing run (x G5/compute nodes) to estimate #GPUs.

Initial sizing (very rough):
- If majority of traffic is 8–12k: a dedicated pool of ~6x A100-80GB (or comparable) with autoscale cushion should meet 150req/s and 120 concurrent with streaming, assuming batched decode optimizations and KV cache.
- If 20–30% of traffic hits 32k regularly: add an extra 2–3 GPUs or use a mixed pool with a few high-memory nodes to handle tails.

Immediate risks / items to validate:
- Need sample prompt sets to confirm average token lengths and document sizes.
- Confirm model family and whether FinCo will accept an open-source model variant (e.g., Llama-family / Mistral) or requires a specific licensed model.

Next steps / timeline:
- Alex: share sample prompts and a small corpus (S3/Drive link).
- FinCo + Redwood: agree on a 90-min benchmark window. We'll run the replay and return a perf report within 72 hours of data receipt.
- Post-run: review tail latencies and propose production config (dedicated pool + routing policy + cache settings).

If helpful, we can also show a short demo of streaming behaviors and how first-byte tuning works (warm KV, early-token decode).

— Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
